title: Liapoldus Core plugin traffic boundary
core: A single Core stores desired plugin configuration in SQLite and exposes Management API. V1 connects to manually started plugins at fixed registered endpoints; v2 adds external Docker/Swarm/Kubernetes placement and replica self-registration without Core workload management. The operator installs and updates workloads; Core never provides install or process-management APIs and does not serve or proxy public traffic.

serverPlugin.process: One separate Server plugin instance per Core in v1; Caddy is built into the plugin, never into Core.
serverPlugin.configSource: Versioned plugin JSON settings stored by Core and pulled by the plugin from Core REST after Reload(generation); the plugin compiles JSON into its private Caddy runtime configuration.
serverPlugin.persistentState: ACME/CertMagic state and site releases use the Server plugin persistent filesystem; current/previous site release pointers remain plugin-owned.
serverPlugin.listeners: Server plugin opens its own public listeners. Core does not embed Caddy, launch a second Caddy binary or pass public listener sockets.

pluginDataProtocol.call: Plugins register and invoke plugin-defined generic peer methods; product payload contracts remain owned by participating plugins.
pluginDataProtocol.registration: pluginprotocol exposes generic plugin-defined method/handler registration without predeclared product RPCs.
pluginDataProtocol.pluginToPlugin: Plugins call explicitly allowed peer instances directly over the independently configured authenticated pluginprotocol transport; Core distributes policy over Plugin SDK REST and is not a payload proxy.

pluginAdminArtifactUpload.request: multipart/form-data with JSON metadata and one declared binary artifact
pluginAdminArtifactUpload.coreBehavior: count received bytes and stream artifact to the authorized plugin action without buffering the complete artifact
pluginAdminArtifactUpload.transport: generic Plugin SDK REST artifact endpoint; not a Caddy-specific Core endpoint

activation: Core validates candidate bytes before a transaction, atomically promotes them to active and shifts the former active to previous, then calls REST Reload. Each plugin pulls the exact generation and ACKs its digest; partial application is roll-forward with per-replica fencing, not compensation.
configuration: User traffic and plugin-specific configuration are never read from SQLite per request; Core serves active in-memory generations.
ha: Core is one instance and Server plugin is one active v1 instance; PostgreSQL, S3 and shared-storage HA are not required.
